_note: The Gym manifest (WP25a): which grammar points act as selectable form categories, grouped into picker columns. 'point' must match the grammar point title exactly (resolved to ids at request time). 'usage' is the plain-language hover explanation; 'example' is a short illustration. 'nonstandard': forms hidden behind the 'include non-standard words' toggle.

entries.label: Present -are
entries.usage: Now or regularly, -are verbs.
entries.example: Io parlo italiano.

entries.label: Present -ere/-ire
entries.usage: Now or regularly, -ere and -ire verbs.
entries.example: Prendo il treno.

entries.label: Passato prossimo (avere)
entries.usage: A finished past with avere.
entries.example: Ho mangiato una mela.

entries.label: Passato prossimo (essere)
entries.usage: Past with essere — motion and reflexives.
entries.example: È partita presto.

entries.label: Imperfect
entries.usage: The ongoing or habitual past.
entries.example: Giocavo sempre.

entries.label: Future
entries.usage: What will happen.
entries.example: Domani mangerò tardi.

entries.label: Conditional
entries.usage: What would happen.
entries.example: Vorrei partire.

entries.label: Subjunctive
entries.usage: After che — wish, doubt, opinion.
entries.example: Penso che tu venga.

entries.label: Imperative
entries.usage: Commands.
entries.example: Parla più forte!

entries.label: Progressive
entries.usage: Happening right now.
entries.example: Sto mangiando adesso.

entries.label: Essere (present)
entries.usage: For saying who or what someone is, and how things are, right now.
entries.example: Io sono studente. — I am a student.

entries.label: Avere (present)
entries.usage: For what you have — and in Italian also for being hungry, thirsty, right, or a certain age.
entries.example: Io ho vent'anni. — I am twenty years old.

entries.label: Negation
entries.usage: To say you don't do something: non sits straight in front of the verb and nothing else moves.
entries.example: Io non parlo inglese. — I don't speak English.

entries.point: C'è and ci sono — there is / there are
entries.label: C'è, ci sono
entries.usage: For saying what is there — one of it, or several.
entries.example: C'è un libro sul tavolo. — There is a book on the table.

entries.label: Reflexives
entries.usage: For what you do to yourself — washing, getting up, getting dressed.
entries.example: Ogni mattina mi alzo alle sette. — Every morning I get up at seven.

entries.label: Trapassato prossimo
entries.usage: For what had already happened before something else happened in the past.
entries.example: Quando sei arrivato, io avevo già mangiato. — When you arrived, I had already eaten.

entries.label: Reported speech
entries.usage: For passing on what somebody else said or asked.
entries.example: Mi ha detto che è stanco. — He told me (that) he is tired.

entries.point: The passive voice (essere/venire; il si passivante)
entries.label: Passive
entries.usage: When what happened to something matters more than who did it.
entries.example: La lettera è scritta in italiano. — The letter is written in Italian.

entries.label: Hypotheticals
entries.usage: For imagining something that isn't so: if I had time, I would come.
entries.example: Se avessi tempo, andrei al cinema. — If I had time, I would go to the cinema.

entries.label: Gerund
entries.usage: For the -ing form: doing one thing while, or by, doing another.
entries.example: È caduto correndo dietro all'autobus. — He fell while running after the bus.

entries.label: Subjunctive after benché
entries.usage: Linking words like although, before and so that always pull a special verb form after them.
entries.example: Benché faccia freddo, escono lo stesso. — Although it's cold, they go out anyway.

entries.label: Past hypotheticals
entries.usage: For imagining a past that never happened: if I had known, I would have come.
entries.example: Se avessi saputo, sarei venuto prima. — If I had known, I would have come earlier.

entries.label: Past subjunctive
entries.usage: After I think or I thought, when the thing you are thinking about already happened.
entries.example: Credo che lui abbia già mangiato. — I think he has already eaten.

entries.label: Passato remoto
entries.usage: The past of stories, novels and history — and of everyday speech in the south.
entries.example: Il re costruì un grande palazzo. (racconto) — The king built a great palace. (narrative)

entries.point: Key irregular presents (vado, faccio, posso, voglio)
entries.label: Irregular presents
entries.usage: The handful of everyday verbs that break the pattern: go, do, can, want.
entries.example: Io vado al mercato adesso. — I'm going to the market now.

entries.label: Definite article
entries.usage: il/lo/la/i/gli/le.
entries.example: il libro, gli amici

entries.label: Indefinite article
entries.usage: un/uno/una.
entries.example: un cane, uno studente

entries.label: Adjectives
entries.usage: Adjectives match gender and number.
entries.example: una macchina rossa

entries.label: Articulated prepositions
entries.usage: preposition + article fused.
entries.example: del pane, nel bosco

entries.label: Possessive/demonstrative
entries.usage: il mio, questo/quello.
entries.example: il mio libro, questa sera

entries.label: Subject pronouns
entries.usage: The words for I, you, he and she — needed only when you want to stress who, since the verb ending already says it.
entries.example: Io sono di Roma. — I am from Rome.

entries.label: Noun gender/number
entries.usage: Whenever you name a thing: it is either masculine or feminine, and its ending changes for more than one.
entries.example: Ho due libri. — I have two books.

entries.label: Question words
entries.usage: For asking anything that needs more than a yes or a no — where, how, what, when, why.
entries.example: Dove abiti? — Where do you live?

entries.point: Direct object pronouns (lo, la, li, le…)
entries.label: Direct pronouns
entries.usage: For a person or thing already mentioned, so you don't name it twice: I know him, I'm buying them.
entries.example: Conosci Marco? Sì, lo conosco bene. — Do you know Marco? Yes, I know him well.

entries.point: Indirect pronouns, ci and ne (gli, le, ci, ne)
entries.label: Indirect, ci, ne
entries.usage: For saying to him, to her, there, or some of it without repeating what you mean.
entries.example: Telefono a Paolo; gli telefono stasera. — I'm calling Paolo; I'll call him tonight.

entries.label: Comparatives
entries.usage: For saying one thing is bigger, smaller or better than another — or the best of the lot.
entries.example: Roma è più grande di Firenze. — Rome is bigger than Florence.

entries.label: Combined pronouns
entries.usage: When you say both the thing and the person it goes to, and the two little words meet.
entries.example: Il libro? Glielo do domani. — The book? I'll give it to him tomorrow.

entries.label: Relative pronouns
entries.usage: For gluing two statements about the same thing into one: the man who lives nearby.
entries.example: È l'uomo che abita qui vicino. — That's the man who lives nearby.

entries.label: Irregular comparatives
entries.usage: For better and worse, which have their own words instead of the usual pattern.
entries.example: Questo ristorante è migliore dell'altro. — This restaurant is better than the other.

entries.label: Connectors
entries.usage: For tying ideas together in writing or a careful argument: so, however, since, besides.
entries.example: Piove, quindi restiamo a casa. — It's raining, so we're staying home.

entries.point: Focus & dislocation (è a Roma che…, ce l'ho)
entries.label: Focus & dislocation
entries.usage: For pushing the important part of what you say to the front, the way speech does.
entries.example: È a Roma che vivo, non a Milano. — It's in Rome that I live, not Milan.

entries.label: Formal register
entries.usage: For letters, business and anything official, where the everyday wording sounds too casual.
entries.example: A mio avviso, la proposta è valida. — In my opinion, the proposal is sound.
